finding_dispositions.evidence: Fresh r7 verifier rebuild/replay and targeted tests passed for no-follow initialization, fanout, and post-initialization objects/staging/locks/resources replacement. Descriptor-bound operations reject replaced attested ancestors before external mutation.

The fresh r7 clock regression passed: expiry observation persists repository-owned high-water state, and subsequent clock rollback cannot revive an expired lease. Authoritative time decisions remain transactionally bound to persisted high-water state.

Fresh canonical resource-order and opposing-process tests passed for the existing lock API. Cross-token acquisition rejects decreasing resource sequences, and opposing two-process requests terminate without deadlock.

The fresh exact claim/reconciliation regression passed. Direct CommitBatch validation binds the complete ordered lease-resource set, fence tokens, task lease, and same-transaction event payload, including missing, extra, empty, stale, and wrong-lease rejection.

Fresh connection tests passed for doctor and backup read-only enforcement. Read-only URI, query_only, and deny-by-default authorizer reject direct writes and WITH-prefixed UPDATE, DELETE, and INSERT statements.

Fresh replay and recovery corruption tests passed. Event indexes, transaction revisions, transaction heads, and task/head state are validated against authoritative replay and fail closed on corruption.

Independent r7 fresh-object probes at object.after_staging_directory_fsync and object.after_publication fail closed, clear wrong staging/final names, and leave no available metadata. Post-commit replacement persists quarantined metadata and clears the wrong final.

Fresh r7 stateful dedup regressions at object.after_object_directory_fsync and object.before_metadata_commit passed: the current transaction rolls back, preexisting available metadata is durably quarantined in a separate transaction, and wrong final/staging names are cleared. Normal dedup and fresh/post-commit paths also passed.

The gate-bound two-writer regression passed at both mismatch windows: writer B is finitely blocked by the same-digest exclusive publication lock while writer A is in stale cleanup, then succeeds after A releases; final bytes remain readable, metadata is available, and staging is empty. An independent fork probe confirmed the exact publication resource is process-exclusive. Cleanup records the mismatch device/inode and an independent replacement-before-cleanup probe confirmed that a later different inode is not unlinked.

The new publication lock is acquired as a hidden ordinary resource named object-publication:<digest>. ADR-0002 requires an action to retain all call-span resource locks until its raw receipt object is durable. In an independent probe, after acquiring installation shared and the legitimate resource task:task-1, acquiring the publication resource failed with RepositoryConfigurationError because object-publication sorts before task and violates the complete held resource sequence. Calling public put_verified under the same required locks also failed with global lock-order violation because it unconditionally reacquires installation. Resource IDs are unrestricted, and put_verified accepts no pre-acquired lock context, so receipt persistence is not composable with the governing call-span protocol.

findings.summary: The hidden per-digest resource lock makes public object publication incompatible with ADR-0002 call-span resource locks and dependent on business resource lexicographic values.
findings.evidence: ADR-0002 requires installation shared, the complete canonical action resource lock set, then object shared, and requires raw receipt durability before releasing the action locks. r7 put_verified always starts by acquiring installation and then separately acquires resource:object-publication:<digest>. With installation shared plus resource:task:task-1 already held, direct acquisition of the hidden publication resource raised 'resource locks must increase across the complete held sequence' because object-publication sorts before task. Invoking put_verified in that same valid outer context raised 'global repository lock order was violated' on its attempted installation reacquisition. The public API has no way to accept or recognize the existing installation/resource context or acquire the publication identity in the original atomic sorted group. Thus a required receipt flow cannot use the public repository contract, and behavior would vary with otherwise valid resource ID spelling.
findings.required_fix: Make same-digest serialization composable with the governing call-span lock context. Either add a distinct attested publication-lock tier ordered after the complete action resource set and before object-maintenance, or provide a lock-context-aware publication primitive that includes the digest identity in one upfront canonical acquisition and does not reacquire held installation/resources. Preserve cross-thread/process same-digest exclusion and inode-bound cleanup. Add gate-bound tests that hold installation plus action resources lexicographically both below and above the publication identity, persist a raw receipt through the supported public/context API before releasing them, and prove finite opposing-process behavior with no rank inversion, reentrancy failure, or partial lock acquisition.
